chunks.text:
## Indoor instrument

An instrument explicitly classified as indoor may continue during a wind suspension, provided its own safety interlocks remain closed. A roof visible as closed on the calendar does not establish indoor classification.

record.description: An explicitly indoor-classified instrument may continue during wind suspension if its own safety interlocks remain closed. A roof shown as closed on the calendar does not establish indoor classification.

chunks.text:
## Suspension

Suspend outdoor observations when the wind interlock opens. Preserve reservation identifiers during suspension. Resume only after the interlock closes and the duty operator records a restart approval.

record.description: An open wind interlock requires suspending outdoor observations while preserving reservation identifiers. Resumption requires the interlock to close and the duty operator to record restart approval.

chunks.text:
## Forecast display

The forecast panel predicts wind for planning. A favourable forecast is not an interlock signal and cannot authorize a restart.

record.description: The forecast panel predicts wind for planning. A favourable forecast is neither an interlock signal nor authorization to restart.

chunks.text:
## Training slots

Daytime training slots can be reassigned by an instructor without the night-time approval workflow. This shortcut does not apply to confirmed observations.

record.description: An instructor may reassign daytime training slots without the night-time approval workflow. This shortcut does not apply to confirmed observations.

chunks.text:
## Planner

The planner solves interval conflicts using instrument availability and reservation priority. It can compute a plan while execution is suspended. A computed plan is not permission to bypass a weather interlock or clock check.

record.description: The planner resolves interval conflicts using instrument availability and reservation priority, even while execution is suspended. A computed plan cannot bypass a weather interlock or clock check.

chunks.text:
## Prototype recovery

The retired prototype cleared pending reservations when time drifted and restarted on its first local clock sample. These behaviours must not be used to recover the current gateway.

record.description: The retired prototype cleared pending reservations on time drift and restarted on its first local clock sample. These behaviours must not be used for current gateway recovery.

chunks.text:
## Timezones

Observers may display the same reservation in different timezones. The stored start time and reservation identifier remain unchanged. Calendar export is a view, not a gateway command.

record.description: Observers can view a reservation in different timezones without changing its stored start time or identifier. Calendar export is a view rather than a gateway command.

chunks.text:
# Calendar display

The calendar is a read-only projection of reservation and instrument state.

record.description: The calendar provides a read-only projection of reservation and instrument state.

chunks.text:
## Locked instrument

If the instrument has an active maintenance lock, leave the transfer pending even after observer acceptance and operator approval. The lock must be cleared by the instrument team first.

record.description: An active instrument maintenance lock keeps a transfer pending even after observer acceptance and operator approval. The instrument team must clear the lock first.

chunks.text:
## Simulation clock

The simulator advances time manually and never waits for reference checks. Its accelerated clock is isolated from the real instrument gateway.

record.description: The simulator advances time manually without waiting for reference checks. Its accelerated clock is isolated from the real instrument gateway.

chunks.text:
## Services

The reservation service accepts requests, a planner assigns intervals, and an instrument gateway executes approved schedules. The calendar displays plans but cannot authorize execution.

record.description: The reservation service accepts requests, the planner assigns intervals, and the instrument gateway executes approved schedules. The calendar displays plans but cannot authorize execution.

chunks.text:
# Scheduler architecture

Meridian separates ownership, planning, execution and display to permit independent restarts.

record.description: Meridian separates ownership, planning, execution, and display so that they can restart independently.

chunks.text:
# Meridian scheduler

Meridian schedules shared observatory instruments. Reservation rules below concern confirmed night-time observations, not daytime training sessions.

record.description: Meridian schedules shared observatory instruments. The reservation rules concern confirmed night-time observations rather than daytime training sessions.

chunks.text:
# Confirmed reservations

These rules apply to confirmed night-time reservations on shared instruments.

For orientation, the reservation console links to the calendar's [colour legend](calendar.md#colours).

record.description: The reservation rules apply to confirmed night-time reservations on shared instruments. An orientation link points to the calendar colour legend from the reservation console.

chunks.text:
## Clock offset

If the absolute clock offset exceeds two seconds, pause schedule execution and notify the duty operator. Keep queued reservations unchanged. Resume only after two consecutive reference checks report an offset within two seconds.

record.description: An absolute clock offset exceeding two seconds requires pausing schedule execution and notifying the duty operator while leaving queued reservations unchanged. Resumption requires two consecutive reference checks with an offset within two seconds.

chunks.text:
## Missing reference

If the reference clock is unavailable, keep execution paused; a local clock reading alone cannot satisfy either recovery check.

record.description: Execution remains paused when the reference clock is unavailable. A local clock reading alone cannot satisfy either recovery check.

chunks.text:
## Colours

Amber indicates a pending assignment, blue a confirmed slot, and grey a suspended interval. Changing a browser theme changes colours locally without changing instrument execution. A visual refresh cannot clear a maintenance lock.

record.description: Calendar colours indicate pending assignments, confirmed slots, and suspended intervals with amber, blue, and grey respectively. Browser theme changes affect colours locally without changing execution, and a visual refresh cannot clear a maintenance lock.

chunks.text:
# Time coordination

The gateway compares instrument time with the observatory reference before executing a schedule.

record.description: The gateway compares instrument time against the observatory reference before executing a schedule.

chunks.text:
## Transfer

Transfer a reservation only after the receiving observer accepts it and the duty operator approves the transfer. Retain the original reservation identifier and record both observers in the audit trail. A transfer does not alter the [weather suspension](weather.md#suspension).

record.description: Transferring a reservation requires acceptance by the receiving observer and approval by the duty operator, retaining the original identifier and recording both observers in the audit trail. Transfer does not alter weather suspension.

chunks.text:
## Navigation

Read [Transfer](reservations.md#transfer), [Weather](weather.md#suspension), and [Clock](clock.md#clock-offset) for operational details. The calendar's [colours](calendar.md#colours) are display conventions.

record.description: This navigation section links to transfer, weather suspension, and clock offset operational details. It also points to calendar colours as display conventions.
